newsitem.title: UK: Analysts see T&N sticking with Kolbenschmidt.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see T&N sticking with Kolbenschmidt.

text.p: Share analysts watching components group T&N Plc's labours to buy into German piston maker Kolbenschmidt AG said on Friday that a report from Germany that T&N had allowed a share option in Kolbenschmidt to lapse need not imply the end of the British firm's ambitions.

Earlier, T&N said it was not making any comment on a report in the Boersen Zeitung newspaper that it had not extended an option contract with Commerzbank AG that gave it the right to buy a 24.99 percent block of Kolbenschmidt shares.
This contract had been due to expire on December 31, 1996.
In conjunction with an identical option with another bank running until September 1997, the option would have given T&N total ongoing rights over 49.9 percent of the German firm.

T&N's attempts to buy Kolbenschmidt date back to 1995, when Germany's cartel office stepped in and blocked the entire approach on competition grounds. It has appealed the ruling but is prevented from holding any stake, including 24.99 percent.

"Obviously we don't know what T&N has done (with Commerzbank), but we would be amazed if T&N were to walk away from Kolbenschmidt at this stage," said an engineering analyst at one London brokerage who declined to be named.

Despite its silence on Friday, there was little doubt that T&N intended to clarify its position in due course. When it fixed the September 1997 option last month it promised to make an announcement "shortly" about the Commerzbank shares.
In the meantime, investors appeared ready to wait and see on Friday, and T&N shares firmed slightly during the morning.
The shares rose 2.0 pence to 173 pence.

Asked why he thought the T&N stock price had responded calmly to the German report, analyst Robert Speed at Henderson Crosthwaite said he believed investors would regard taking a 25 percent stake as reasonably sound tactic by the British firm.
"I think the UK equity market would welcome T&N being able to take a 25 percent stake as a potential precursor to a joint venture, for example," Speed told Reuters.
Kolbenschmidt, which also makes bearings, is strongly placed in the German automotive market.

T&N chairman Sir Colin Hope has said for over a year that his firm would try several alternative ways to buy into Kolbenschmidt to achieve what he has called "the considerable financial benefits that would flow from this transaction".
